messages.subject: Price-volume plot with ggplot
parts:
Dear all,

Let say I have the followings data:

Dat1 = structure(list(Date = structure(c(15670, 15671, 15672, 15673,
+ 15674, 15677, 15678, 15679, 15680, 15670, 15671, 15672, 15673,
+ 15674, 15677, 15678, 15679, 15680), class = "Date"), Price = c(37.47,
+ 37.34, 37.97, 38.34, 38.29, 37.92, 38.13, 38.66, 38.32, 33.97,
+ 33.62, 33.62, 33.93, 34.13, 34.14, 33.92, 33.91, 33.65), Volume = c(3283000,
+ 3435400, 3454000, 3970800, 2406200, 2714500, 2188400, 3927500,
+ 3568700, 34852800, 26506100, 30828500, 29542600, 36130600, 19611800,
+ 21290900, 29170900, 23415000), Asset = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L,
+ 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("A",
+ "B"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("Date", "Price", "Volume",
+ "Asset"), row.names = c(NA, 18L), class = "data.frame")


Now with this data, I would like to have a plot as given in
'http://www.simple-talk.com/content/print.aspx?article=1351' (please
see the first plot).

Basically in my plot there will be 2 parts in my plotting window. In
the upper part, I will have price-series (just time series plot). And
in the lower part, I will plot the Volumes (as small bar-charts). And
2 Assets "A" & "B" will be distinguished by 2 different colors.

Can somebody throw me some pointer how to achieve that with ggplot?

Thanks for your help.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Price-volume plot with ggplot
parts:
Hi:

You don't have enough information to do the top plot - you need the
daily min and max as well as the opening value to associate with the
tick. Those values are not represented in Dat1 - I don't know what
Price represents. Basically, you would need to apply geom_segment()
for both the vertical range and the horizontal tick in the price
chart. The bar chart would be much simpler in principle. A few things:

(i) The y-axis for both plots will be on the left rather than the right.
(ii) You'll need to make some adjustments to compensate for the large
difference in value ranges between price and volume, because by
default the two y-axis lines will not be aligned.
(iii) Use scale_x_date() to attune the date scale (you may need to use
the scales package).
(iv) Look into grid.arrange() in gridExtra or the approach used in
section 8.4 of the ggplot2 book to stitch the two plots together.

This should already be available in the quantmod or xts packages, but
if you're just curious about how it can be done in ggplot2, it's
certainly possible and not all that hard.

Dennis

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Price-volume plot with ggplot
parts:
Christopher,

I see Dennis's response noting there's not enough data here, but when
you have all the required data, you'll want to first generate the two
plots, and then, as he notes, use something like gridExtra to arrange
them on a page. Just using the data you posted, e.g.:

# Hi-lo plot
p1 <- ggplot(Dat1,aes(Date,Price)) +
stat_summary(fun.ymax="max",fun.ymin="min",geom="pointrange",fun.y="mean")

# Volume plot
p2 <- ggplot(Dat1,aes(Date,Volume,group=Asset))+geom_bar(aes(fill=Asset),stat="identity")

# Dark ages example: arrange using grid, not gridExtra
library( grid )
grid.newpage()
pushViewport( viewport( layout=grid.layout( 3, 1 ) ) )
vplayout<-function( x, y ) viewport( layout.pos.row=x, layout.pos.col=y )
print( p1, vp=vplayout( 1:2,1 ) )
print( p2, vp=vplayout( 2, 1 ) )


Ben

messages.subject: Re: Price-volume plot with ggplot
parts:
On Fri, Dec 7, 2012 at 12:14 PM, Christofer Bogaso
<bogaso.c...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Dennis for your suggestion.
>
> However just to mention that, I do not need max-min plotting. That is
> why I said, I just need the the ****Time series plot for the
> Price"""". Means, in the top part just the Time series and in the
> bottom part just the bar plot.

OK. Here are a couple of ways you could go, which will illustrate some
of the issues that arise with trading days as dates, as well as
legends and scales. I'm using the technique outlined in section 8.4 of
the ggplot2 book to size the two plots. There's a way to do this in
gridExtra::grid.arrange() as well, but I don't have the time to
investigate it right now.

## Stab 1: Treat dates as 'numeric'

library(ggplot2)
library(grid) # needed for the plot layouts below

In this version of the plot, the legend for lines was pulled inside
the graph and the legend for the bar chart was suppressed. By default,
there will be a separate legend for each plot because Asset is mapped
to different aesthetics. I am also plotting volume in millions in an
attempt to align the dates on the plots. Otherwise, the borders of the
two graphs would not be aligned without resorting to trickery.

p1 <- ggplot(Dat1, aes(x = Date, y = Price, colour = Asset)) +
theme_bw() +
geom_line(aes(group = Asset), size = 1) + labs(x = "") +
theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
legend.position = c(0.85, 0.5))

p2 <- ggplot(Dat1, aes(x = Date, y = Volume/1e6, fill = Asset)) +
theme_bw() +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
labs(y = "Volume (millions)") +
scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%m/%d")) +
scale_fill_discrete(guide = "none")

# Set up a grid graphics page
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(20, 1)))

# Define a function to set up the layout of the two plots
vplayout <- function(x, y)
viewport(layout.pos.row = x, layout.pos.col = y)

# Print them
print(p1, vp = vplayout(1:15, 1))
print(p2, vp = vplayout(15:20, 1))

The obvious problem with this plot is the missing days on the weekends
and there is no easy way around this if one wants to maintain
'continuous' time. Since the non-trading days are not represented in
Dat1, ggplot2's default in line graphs is to connect the missing dates
with a linear interpolator, which will be constant if Friday's closing
price is equal to Monday's opening price. OTOH, the missing dates in
the bar chart will create gaps.

Another problem is that the dates are not perfectly aligned: the
points in the line graph align with the left edge of the bars, while
the vertical grid lines in the bar chart line up with the centers of
the bars.

# Stab 2: convert Date to a factor

This time, create a new factor in Dat1 corresponding to dates and redo
the plots. This time the default legends are kept in the result for
reference.

Dat1$Date2 <- factor(format(Dat1$Date, "%m/%d"))

p3 <- ggplot(Dat1, aes(x = Date2, y = Price, colour = Asset)) +
theme_bw() +
geom_line(aes(group = Asset), size = 1) + labs(x = "") +
theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
p4 <- ggplot(Dat1, aes(x = Date2, y = Volume/1e6, fill = Asset)) +
theme_bw() +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
labs(y = "Volume (millions)")

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(20, 1)))

print(p3, vp = vplayout(1:15, 1))
print(p4, vp = vplayout(15:20, 1))

You could play with scale_x_discrete() in p4 if you wanted to reduce
the number of factor levels plotted (see the breaks = argument), but
for long series, this might be problematic - e.g., if you wanted to
label the first trading day of a week or month, you would probably
need an indicator in the data set for that property and use it in
defining the breaks = argument of the scale_ function.


There are tools in place to produce something more visually appealing
like the graphics in quantmod, PerformanceAnalytics or xts, but it
would take a bit of work to get there (e.g., a new theme function for
this class of graphic, and perhaps a customized date scale and/or
legend guide).

Hope this is enough to get you started...
Dennis
